# Mac Pulse 1.5.2
- Removed the Insights and Connectivity tabs to simplify navigation. System readings, pressure indicators and configurable alert rules remain available in the dashboard and Settings. - Removed the unused Insights processing and on-demand connection-check code. - Existing tab layouts retain their order and hidden-tab choices for the remaining tabs. Retired tabs are ignored when loading older preferences. - Updated the README and monitoring screenshots to show the current navigation.
Existing monitoring history, storage snapshots, alert rules and Cleanup state are retained.
Requires an Apple Silicon Mac running macOS 14.2 or newer. This build uses free ad hoc signing and is not Apple-notarized.

# Mac Pulse 1.5.1
- The top navigation now adapts to the window width. Wide windows show every tab label; narrower windows use compact icon tabs while keeping the selected tab's name visible. - All tabs remain accessible without cut-off labels or horizontal scrolling. Hover over a compact tab to see its name, or use the All tabs menu. - Custom tab order and hidden tabs are preserved. Exported dashboard images use the same adaptive navigation.
The seven features introduced in 1.5.0 remain included. Existing settings, monitoring history and Cleanup state are retained.
Requires an Apple Silicon Mac running macOS 14.2 or newer. This build uses free ad hoc signing and is not Apple-notarized.

# Mac Pulse 1.5.0
- **Insights:** see sustained resource findings with links to the relevant app or chart, plus pressure, swap, available disk and Mac Pulse's own usage. - **Storage growth:** track folders with local snapshots, compare complete scans and use a clickable storage map. Partial scans cannot produce misleading growth comparisons. - **Alert rules:** configure thresholds, duration and optional app selection, including low disk space, memory pressure and CPU temperature. Set quiet hours for notifications. - **Cleanup History:** inspect receipts and restore tracked items still in Trash. Restore verifies identity and the original folder and never overwrites existing files. Protected Trash locations or original folders may require Full Disk Access; denied access is explained and leaves the item in Trash. - **App files:** review an app bundle and exact bundle-ID matches for caches, preferences, support data and saved state. Associated files require explicit selection and removal rechecks activity and file identity. - **Connectivity:** run DNS, latency, packet-loss and HTTPS checks on demand. - **Keep readings visible:** enable independent menu-bar items and a movable floating dashboard from Settings → Menu Bar.
Folder scans and network checks run only when requested. History and preferences stay local. Existing app settings and monitoring/Cleanup history are retained.
Requires an Apple Silicon Mac running macOS 14.2 or newer. This build uses free ad hoc signing and is not Apple-notarized; macOS may require approval for the first downloaded installation.

# Mac Pulse 1.4.0
- Mac Pulse now checks for updates daily and offers a native update dialog with release notes, Install, Later and Skip options. - Check manually from the Mac Pulse app menu, the menu-bar panel or Settings → Updates. - Settings → Updates lets you disable automatic checks or opt in to automatic downloads and installation. - Update feeds and downloads are signed and verified before extraction. Monitoring and cleanup data are never sent with update checks. - Your existing settings, monitoring history and Cleanup state are retained.
**One-time upgrade:** versions 1.3.1 and earlier do not contain the updater. Quit the earlier app, download this release and replace it in Applications once. Subsequent releases can update inside Mac Pulse.
Requires an Apple Silicon Mac running macOS 14.2 or newer. This build uses free ad hoc signing and is not Apple-notarized; macOS may require approval for the first downloaded installation.
